source variant: NP 1933 inequality p0 <= k p1 (p. 300, eq. 25) identified as the same ordering with c = 1/k

Section/unit mismatch: section 169.1 is titled 'Sampling models, estimands, statistics and identifiability', but the owed unit is 'Hypothesis tests and confidence sets'; the routed chapter and its annex contain no treatment of estimands or identifiability (neither term occurs). Components were assessed as mapped; the section-title topics are not evidenced by this unit.

C007: 'choose j ... with P(K>j) <= alpha <= P(K>=j)' presupposes such j exists; neither the entry nor annex:p15.binomial.most.powerful writes the existence argument, and the entry does not restate the range of alpha (taken from def:p15-statistical-experiment). Trivial, not graded.

C008: the count threshold rule is asserted to be 'exactly a likelihood-ratio test' and thm:p15-neyman-pearson is invoked, but that theorem's phi* is 'the preceding exact-size test'; the threshold c = L(j) and the fact that the Neyman-Pearson proof uses only the threshold form plus exact size are left implicit.

C005: the c = 0 clause ('a smaller size can attain the same power') rests on a one-sentence remark; the competitor 1{f1 > 0}, its size P0(f1 > 0) <= alpha, and the condition P0(f1 > 0) < alpha for strictness are not written. Not graded: the remark plus the proved characterization supports the possibility claim.

C010: 'The lower-tail versions have the same properties' - the lower-tail p-values P0(T' <= t) and P0(T' < t) + u P0(T' = t) are not displayed; they are fixed only implicitly by the order reversal in annex 316-318 and are later used for F_{n,p}(k) in annex 609-621.

C012: joint measurability of the integrated test int_0^1 delta_t(x,u) du is given as a compressed monotone-class outline without citing the route's own thm:p15-section-measures / thm:p15-tonelli (product-measures.tex 143-181), which supply it.

C006 source fidelity: NP 1933 p. 300 extends the boundary condition to 'every point on the complete boundary S' and obtains stationarity from the unconditioned minimum of P0 - kP1 (p. 298, eq. 17); the handbook lemma keeps the conclusion local and takes stationarity as hypothesis (annex 183-185 disclaims a Lagrange multiplier). Not graded: the entry promises only the local condition, and a minimizing variation is stationary.
